items.title: Ellen Rowe interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 2, 2024
items.q: we had her out to Connecticut, had her out here to Michigan... I set the whole thing up... I feel like I’m off the hook

ctx.x: Um hum. Yeah, she was a great ambassador for the music, we had her out to Connecticut, had her out here to Michigan, and she had an ongoing relationship with a high school out in Long Island and I used to go out and kind of oversee those residencies with the band director and she would just come in and work with any level of student that was there, she would play with them and she was just so gracious. One favorite McPartland story of mine is that she came out to the University of Michigan and the dean and…

Oh. Did she ever tell you about the time her uncle came from England, you know, an aristocratic type person and came to where she was playing. And he goes, “Margaret! Do your parents know what you’re doing here?” It was so funny the way she said it, you know like what are you doing in a bar.

Well I mean of course the thing that’s legendary, one of the many things that’s legendary about Marian was just the mouth on her that you would never guess in a million years sitting on the Piano Jazz show, but you get her backstage with her band or in the green room or whatever, and oh my God, I mean she had a mouth on her and she was not afraid to let all kinds of “blue” things fly.
